title: Add holistic causal-window ensemble detector with progressive quarantine and deferred cutover protector
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: we continue to see gradual, correlated latency degradations that slip through percentile-only canaries and later manifest as tail regressions under production load. This PR introduces a holistic causal-window ensemble detector that fuses short- and medium-horizon signals (latency percentiles, throughput deltas, and request-shape fingerprints) using a causal weighting window and a conservative progressive quarantine policy to contain regressions early without causing noisy rollbacks. It also adds a deferred cutover protector that prevents hard cutovers when ensemble confidence is marginal and system headroom is low.

What this change does: 
- Implements a CausalWindowEnsemble detector component (canary/detectors/causal_window_ensemble.py) that: computes time-weighted feature vectors, applies causal decay to recent signals, and runs a lightweight ensemble of detectors (quantile drift, throughput derivative, fingerprint divergence).
- Adds progressive_quarantine orchestrator (canary/orchestrator/progressive_quarantine.py) which escalates quarantine levels (probe-only -> partial-route-shed -> full-shed) based on sustained ensemble score and tenant headroom metadata.
- Adds deferred_cutover_protector policy (canary/policies/deferred_cutover.py) which checks model capacity, replica headroom, and ensemble confidence before allowing rollout cutovers; delays by configurable backoff if conditions are not met.
- Exposes new observability metrics and traces (observability/metrics/cw_ensemble_metrics.yaml) and integrates with tracing hooks to attribute which signal triggered quarantine.
- Adds unit and integration tests (canary/tests/test_causal_window.py, canary/tests/test_quarantine_fsm.py) and a lightweight synthetic workload generator (perf/synth/gradual_drift_generator.py) for CI regression tests.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed with SRE and Observability (linked Linear ENG-2345)
- [x] Unit tests covering edge cases for decay windows and ensemble weighting
- [x] Integration tests exercising progressive quarantine escalation and rollback behavior
- [x] Benchmarked default parameters on small cluster; added recommended defaults to docs
- [x] Added metrics and dashboards references for on-call use

Testing & CI: 
Initial CI run: unit tests passed, lint passed, integration tests failed with a flaky timing assertion. Fixed timing window in test harness and re-ran. Final CI: unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, lint: pass, benchmark-smoke: pass. CI summary stored in PR checks.

Rollout plan: 
- Feature is feature-flag gated behind perf_canary.causal_ensemble=true.
- Rolling rollout to canary namespace with 5% traffic for first 24 hours, monitor cw_ensemble.alert_score and progressive_quarantine.action_count.
- If ensemble_score > 0.75 and headroom < 15% for > 10m, policy will hold cutover and escalate to partial route shed; ops playbook created.

Related work: builds on prior ensemble and probe work (ENG-2410) and complements the temporal smoothing changes in perf-canary. This is intentionally conservative: the ensemble favors precision (low false positives) over recall for first rollout.
